messages.text: Team, I just uploaded the client database to the shared folder. Make sure no one shares it outside.
Got it. The file has 500 student records including IDs, emails, and grades. Very sensitive.
We should encrypt it before sharing. I will use our AES+RSA system.
Agreed. Also the API key for the server is: XK92-PLMT-0047-ZZQA. Keep it private.
The admin password was changed to Adm!n@2025#Secure. Only team members should know.
I encrypted the database. SHA-256 verified. Original and decrypted files match perfectly.
Great. Without encryption, anyone intercepting this chat could steal all this data.
Exactly. That is why hybrid encryption AES + RSA is the right approach here.
Did anyone run the performance benchmarks? We need to prove AES is better than DES.
Yes, I just ran it. AES-256 took about 0.002s, while DES was noticeably slower and weaker. AES is definitely hardware optimized.
Make sure you all save the IV and the encrypted AES key in the metadata JSON file. We need them for decryption.
Already done. I used Base64 encoding to convert the binary ciphertext to strings so the JSON does not corrupt.
Here is a dummy credit card test record for the final validation: 4111-2222-3333-4444, exp 12/28, CVV 123. Please run the decryption test on this.
Testing now... The unpad() function removed the PKCS7 padding correctly. Decryption successful and the SHA-256 hash matches 100%.
Perfect work, team. The Cryptography logic is solid and the data is completely secure against unauthorized access.
